Corollary
[positive Ricci curvature at one point forces finite fundamental group]

Source: petersen:page-0321 ↗ thm:pet-ch7-structure-theorem 1. ch7:7.3.14If $(M,g)$ is compact with $\Ric \ge 0$ and $\Ric >0$ on some tangent space $T_pM$, then $\pi _1(M)$ is finite.
Proof

↗ cor:pet-ch7-finite-fundamental-group-positive-ricci \sketch A positive Ricci tensor at one point is incompatible with a nontrivial Euclidean factor in the structure decomposition, since that direction has zero Ricci curvature. Thus the universal cover is compact and the deck group is finite.

□
